(https://llmrecsys.github.io/) The same tutorial reports that formulating various recommendation tasks such as rating prediction, sequential recommendation, straightforward recommendation, and explanation generation into language instructions makes it possible to build universal recommendation engines that can handle different recommendation tasks.

(https://llmrecsys.github.io/) The same tutorial notes that LLMs have a remarkable capacity for understanding natural language, enabling them to comprehend user preferences, item descriptions, and contextual information to generate more accurate and relevant recommendations.

(https://neurips.cc/virtual/2024/poster/93061) These systems face long-tail user and long-tail item challenges, where most users interact with only a handful of items while the majority of items are seldom consumed.
(https://neurips.cc/virtual/2024/poster/93061) These challenges often pose difficulties for existing SRS and can adversely affect user experience and seller benefits.

(https://neurips.cc/virtual/2024/poster/93061) Although a few works have addressed the long-tail challenges, they still struggle with the seesaw or noisy issues due to the intrinsic scarcity of interactions.
(https://neurips.cc/virtual/2024/poster/93061) LLM-ESR is proposed as one of the pioneering approaches that uses LLMs to address long-tail issues from a semantic perspective.
(https://neurips.cc/virtual/2024/poster/93061)

(https://doi.org/10.1145/3589334.3645347) A 2024 paper proposes CLLM4Rec, described as the first generative recommender system that tightly integrates the LLM paradigm and ID paradigm of recommenders.
(https://doi.org/10.1145/3589334.3645347) The approach extends the vocabulary of pretrained LLMs with user and item ID tokens to model user and item collaborative and content semantics.

(https://doi.org/10.1145/3589334.3645347) The same work proposes a soft+hard prompting strategy to effectively learn user/item collaborative and content token embeddings via language modeling on RS-specific corpora.

(https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608889) Traditional recommender systems are renowned for their effectiveness and proficiency within clearly defined domains but are limited in adaptability and incapable of providing recommendations for unexplored data.
(https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608889) LLMs exhibit contextual awareness and strong adaptability to unseen data.

(https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608889) Combining these technologies creates a powerful tool for delivering contextual and relevant recommendations, even in cold scenarios characterized by high data sparsity.
(https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608889) Recommender systems play a pivotal role in delivering personalized recommendations across various domains, from e-commerce to content streaming platforms.
(https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.14524)

(https://www.amazon.science/publications/large-language-models-as-recommender-systems-a-study-of-popularity-bias) Recent advancements have seen the integration of general-purpose Large Language Models into recommendation pipelines.

evidence.title: Recommender Systems in the Era of Large Language Models (LLMs)
evidence.abstract: With the prosperity of e-commerce and web applications, Recommender Systems (RecSys) have become an indispensable and important component in our daily lives, providing personalized suggestions that cater to user preferences. While Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have achieved significant advancements in enhancing recommender systems by modeling user-item interactions and incorporating their textual side information, these DNN-based methods still exhibit some limitations, such as difficulties in effectively understanding users' interests and capturing textual side information, inabilities in generalizing to various seen/unseen recommendation scenarios and reasoning on their predictions, etc. Meanwhile, the development of Large Language Models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT and GPT-4, has revolutionized the fields of Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Artificial Intelligence (AI), due to their remarkable abilities in fundamental responsibilities of language understanding and generation, as well as impressive generalization capabilities and reasoning skills. As a result, recent studies have actively attempted to harness the power of LLMs to enhance recommender systems. Given the rapid evolution of this research direction in recommender systems, there is a pressing need for a systematic overview that summarizes existing LLM-empowered recommender systems, so as to provide researchers and practitioners in relevant fields with an in-depth understanding. Therefore, in this survey, we conduct a comprehensive review of LLM-empowered recommender systems from various aspects including pre-training, fine-tuning, and prompting paradigms. More specifically, we first introduce the representative methods to harness the power of LLMs (as a feature encoder) for learning representations of users and items. Then, we systematically review the emerging advanced techniques of LLMs for enhancing recommender systems from three paradigms, namely pre-training, fine-tuning, and prompting. Finally, we comprehensively discuss the promising future directions in this emerging field.
